newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: "Safe-haven" Singapore dollar gains on Baht float.
newsitem.headline: "Safe-haven" Singapore dollar gains on Baht float.

text.p: The Singapore dollar saw some healthy buying against the U.S. currency on Wednesday thanks to its status as a "safe-haven" currency, dealers said.
The move was in contrast to most of the other Southeast Asian regional currencies, which were reeling from Thailand's move to float the baht, they said.

Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya shocked the Asian currency markets earlier on Wednesday with an announcement that the country's exchange rate would be subject to a managed float, in which the baht's value would be set by market forces with immediate effect.
"We saw quite a bit of selling of the dollar against the Sing following news of the Baht float," a dealer with a European bank said.
"The Sing dollar is believed to be a safe-haven and whenever there is any uncertainty in the region, it will be the best bet," said a dealer with a U.S. bank.
Dealers said activity on the dollar/Sing was "orderly" and not volatile like in some other regional currencies.
"The dip in the dollar against the Sing was very fast and it quickly went back up to Tuesday's levels again," another dealer with a U.S. bank said.
At 0755 GMT, the Singapore dollar was trading at 1.4296/06 to the dollar after hitting an early low of 1.4285 and a high of 1.4300. It was well-supported at 1.4285/90 to the dollar, dealers said.
They said there were no signs of intervention in the open market by Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the de facto central bank.
